---
title: "Case study: leader visits to and from the United States, 1945–2019"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9,
                      fig.height = 5, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(amorem)
source("case-helpers.R")
col_to <- "#178E8E"; col_from <- "#8E7CC3"
```

# Leader visits to and from the United States

`us_leader_visits` lists every visit by a foreign head of state or government
to the United States, and every foreign trip of a US president, from July 1945
to December 2019 (Harvard Dataverse, CC0). Each row is a directed event: the
visitor's country is the `sender`, the host the `receiver`. This case study asks
whether a visit in one direction raises the rate of a visit back, how long that
effect lasts, and how much of a partner's rate is carried by its own past
visits.

## The data

```{r data}
data(us_leader_visits)
v <- us_leader_visits
v$partner <- ifelse(v$sender == "United States", v$receiver, v$sender)
c(visits = nrow(v), to_us = sum(v$direction == "to_us"),
  from_us = sum(v$direction == "from_us"))
```

```{r clean, include = FALSE}
v$year <- as.numeric(format(v$date, "%Y")) + (as.numeric(format(v$date, "%j")) - 0.5) / 366
partners <- sort(table(v$partner), decreasing = TRUE)
```

The `r fmt(nrow(v))` visits involve `r length(partners)` partner countries.
The bundled table uses one name per country across its two source tables (see
`?us_leader_visits`), which reciprocity needs: a visit and the visit back must
name the same partner.

Every event has the United States at one end, so the network is a star. What
the model can learn is **which partner, in which direction, and when**: given
that a foreign leader visits Washington at time *t*, why that country rather
than another; given that the president travels, why to that country.

```{r star, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 7.6, fig.alt = "Radial network: the United States at the centre and its 60 most frequent partners around it, with lines for visits in each direction"}
top <- names(partners)[1:60]
n_to <- table(factor(v$partner[v$direction == "to_us"], levels = top))
n_from <- table(factor(v$partner[v$direction == "from_us"], levels = top))
bal <- as.numeric(n_from) / (as.numeric(n_to) + as.numeric(n_from))   # share of visits by the president
tot <- as.numeric(n_to) + as.numeric(n_from)
o <- order(bal)
ang <- pi / 2 - 0.25 - (2 * pi - 0.5) * (seq_along(top) - 1) / (length(top) - 1)   # clockwise, gap at the top
ang <- setNames(ang, top[o])
x <- cos(ang[top]); y <- sin(ang[top])
ramp <- grDevices::colorRamp(c(col_to, "#C9CDD1", col_from))
pcol <- grDevices::rgb(ramp(bal) / 255)
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2.6, 0.5))
plot(NA, xlim = c(-1.45, 1.45), ylim = c(-1.4, 1.4), asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
for (k in seq_along(top)) {
  b_in <- .bezier(x[k], y[k], 0, 0, 0.10); b_out <- .bezier(0, 0, x[k], y[k], 0.10)
  lines(b_in, col = alpha(col_to, 0.35), lwd = 0.3 + 4.5 * sqrt(n_to[k] / max(n_to)))
  lines(b_out, col = alpha(col_from, 0.45), lwd = 0.3 + 4.5 * sqrt(n_from[k] / max(n_to)))
}
points(x, y, pch = 21, bg = pcol, col = "white", cex = 0.8 + 2.4 * sqrt(tot / max(tot)), lwd = 0.8)
points(0, 0, pch = 21, bg = ink, col = "white", cex = 3.4)
text(0, 0, "US", col = "white", cex = 0.6, font = 2)
lab <- top
r_lab <- 1.06 + 0.03 * sqrt(tot / max(tot))
for (k in seq_along(top)) {
  a <- ang[top[k]]; left <- cos(a) < 0
  text(r_lab[k] * cos(a), r_lab[k] * sin(a), lab[k], cex = 0.5, col = ink,
       srt = if (left) a * 180 / pi - 180 else a * 180 / pi, adj = c(if (left) 1 else 0, 0.5), xpd = TRUE)
}
title_left("Partners send their leaders to Washington more often than presidents visit them",
           "60 most frequent partners, 1945-2019; teal: leader visits to the US; violet: presidential visits; width and dot size grow with visits")
legend("bottomright", title = "dot colour: share of visits by the president", title.adj = 0,
       legend = c("0% (all visits to the US)", "50%", "100%"),
       pt.bg = grDevices::rgb(ramp(c(0, 0.5, 1)) / 255), pch = 21, col = "white", pt.cex = 1.6,
       bty = "n", cex = 0.7, text.col = ink, title.col = ink_soft, xpd = TRUE)
aa <- seq(pi / 2 - 0.2, pi / 2 - 1.1, length.out = 30)
lines(1.33 * cos(aa), 1.33 * sin(aa), col = ink_soft, lwd = 0.9)
n <- length(aa); arrows(1.33 * cos(aa[n - 1]), 1.33 * sin(aa[n - 1]), 1.33 * cos(aa[n]), 1.33 * sin(aa[n]), length = 0.07, col = ink_soft)
text(0.05, 1.38, "clockwise from the top: share of visits by the president, lowest to highest", adj = 0, cex = 0.6, col = ink_soft, xpd = TRUE)
```

```{r star-numbers, include = FALSE}
share_to <- mean(v$direction == "to_us")
n_mostly_to <- sum(bal < 0.5)
most_from <- top[order(-bal)][1:3]
```

Leaders come to the United States more often than presidents travel:
`r pct(share_to)` of the visits are to the US, and `r n_mostly_to` of the 60
partners in the figure send more leaders to Washington than they receive
presidents. The partners whose share of presidential visits is highest are
`r paste(most_from, collapse = ", ")`.

## Visits over time

```{r timeline, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4.4, fig.alt = "Visits per year in each direction, with the presidential terms marked"}
terms <- data.frame(name = c("Truman", "Eisenhower", "Kennedy", "Johnson", "Nixon", "Ford", "Carter",
                             "Reagan", "Bush", "Clinton", "Bush", "Obama", "Trump"),
                    start = c(1945.28, 1953.05, 1961.05, 1963.89, 1969.05, 1974.61, 1977.05,
                              1981.05, 1989.05, 1993.05, 2001.05, 2009.05, 2017.05))
terms$end <- c(terms$start[-1], 2020)
yr <- 1945:2019
to <- table(factor(floor(v$year[v$direction == "to_us"]), levels = yr))
fr <- table(factor(floor(v$year[v$direction == "from_us"]), levels = yr))
par(mar = c(3, 3.4, 2.6, 0.8))
plot(NA, xlim = c(1945, 2020), ylim = c(-max(fr) * 1.15, max(to) * 1.45), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
rect(terms$start, par("usr")[3], terms$end, par("usr")[4], col = c("#F4F6F7", "#FFFFFF"), border = NA)
text((terms$start + terms$end) / 2, par("usr")[4] * 0.97, terms$name, cex = 0.55, col = ink_soft, srt = 90, adj = 1)
rect(yr, 0, yr + 0.85, to, col = col_to, border = NA)
rect(yr, 0, yr + 0.85, -fr, col = col_from, border = NA)
abline(h = 0, col = ink_soft, lwd = 0.6)
axis(1, at = seq(1950, 2020, 10), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
at <- pretty(c(-max(fr), max(to)), 6)
axis(2, at = at, labels = abs(at), las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.7, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
title_left("Visits per year", "above the line: foreign leaders visiting the US; below: presidential visits abroad; bands: presidential terms")
```

```{r timeline-numbers, include = FALSE}
dec <- function(a, b, d) sum(v$year >= a & v$year < b & v$direction == d)
early <- dec(1945, 1960, "to_us") / 15; late <- dec(1990, 2010, "to_us") / 20
```

Visits to the US rise from about `r fmt(early, 0)` a year in 1945–1959 to about
`r fmt(late, 0)` a year in 1990–2009. Presidential travel grows too, and it
comes in bursts: a single trip covers several countries, so several
`from_us` events share a few days.

```{r heat, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 7, fig.alt = "Heatmap of visits by partner and decade, partners ordered by the decade of their peak"}
top40 <- names(partners)[1:40]
dcd <- seq(1940, 2010, 10)
M <- table(factor(v$partner, levels = top40), factor(floor(v$year / 10) * 10, levels = dcd))
M <- M[order(apply(M, 1, which.max), -rowSums(M)), ]
par(mar = c(4.4, 8.5, 2.6, 0.8))
brk <- c(-0.5, 0.5, 1.5, 4.5, 9.5, 19.5, 1e4)
cls <- c("#FFFFFF", "#DCEFEF", "#A9D6D6", "#5FB3B3", "#178E8E", "#0B4F4F")
image(seq_along(dcd), seq_len(nrow(M)), t(M[nrow(M):1, ]), col = cls, breaks = brk, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
abline(v = seq_along(dcd) + 0.5, h = seq_len(nrow(M)) + 0.5, col = "white", lwd = 0.6)
legend("bottom", inset = c(0, -0.115), horiz = TRUE, xpd = TRUE, legend = c("0", "1", "2-4", "5-9", "10-19", "20+"),
       fill = cls, border = "#D5D9DC", bty = "n", cex = 0.6, text.col = ink_soft, title = "visits in the decade", title.col = ink_soft)
axis(1, at = seq_along(dcd), labels = paste0(dcd, "s"), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.72, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
axis(2, at = nrow(M):1, labels = rownames(M), las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.62, col.axis = ink, line = -0.5)
big <- which(M >= 20, arr.ind = TRUE)
text(big[, 2], nrow(M) + 1 - big[, 1], M[big], cex = 0.5, col = "white")
title_left("Visits by partner and decade (both directions)",
           "40 most frequent partners, ordered by the decade of their peak; numbers: cells with 20 or more")
```

```{r heat-numbers, include = FALSE}
peak <- dcd[apply(M, 1, which.max)]; names(peak) <- rownames(M)
first <- dcd[apply(M > 0, 1, which.max)]; names(first) <- rownames(M)
late <- names(peak)[peak >= 2000]; new <- names(first)[first >= 1960]
```

Of the 40 partners, `r sum(peak <= 1980)` have their busiest decade in the
1980s or earlier and `r length(late)` in the 2000s or 2010s
(`r paste(head(late, 8), collapse = ", ")`). `r length(new)` of them have no
visit before 1960, among them `r paste(head(new, 5), collapse = ", ")`.

## Reciprocity: how long after a visit does the visit back come?

For every visit we measure the time since the last visit **in the opposite
direction** with the same partner (`reciprocity_time_recent`). Visits with
no earlier visit in the other direction are counted separately.

```{r lag-data}
ev <- v[order(v$time), c("sender", "receiver", "time", "direction", "partner", "year")]
lag <- endogenous_features(ev, stats = c("reciprocity_time_recent", "recency"))
lag$gap_years <- lag$reciprocity_time_recent / 365.25
tapply(is.na(lag$gap_years), lag$direction, mean)
```

```{r lag, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4.4, fig.alt = "Cumulative distribution of the years since the last visit in the opposite direction, for both directions"}
par(mar = c(3.4, 3.6, 2.6, 0.8))
xs <- 10^seq(-2, log10(60), length.out = 400)
cdf <- function(d) { g <- lag$gap_years[lag$direction == d & !is.na(lag$gap_years)]; ecdf(g)(xs) }
plot(xs, cdf("from_us"), log = "x", type = "l", lwd = 2.4, col = col_from, ylim = c(0, 1),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
lines(xs, cdf("to_us"), lwd = 2.4, col = col_to)
abline(h = 0.5, col = rule)
axis(1, at = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 50), labels = c("4 days", "5 weeks", "1 year", "10 years", "50 years"),
     tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.72, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
axis(2, at = seq(0, 1, 0.25), labels = pct(seq(0, 1, 0.25), 0), las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.7, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.6)
mtext("time since the partner's last visit in the other direction (log scale)", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.72, col = ink_soft)
med <- c(from_us = median(lag$gap_years[lag$direction == "from_us"], na.rm = TRUE),
         to_us = median(lag$gap_years[lag$direction == "to_us"], na.rm = TRUE))
points(med, c(0.5, 0.5), pch = 21, bg = c(col_from, col_to), col = "white", cex = 1.5)
text(med["from_us"], 0.5, sprintf("president travels: median %.1f years", med["from_us"]), pos = 2, cex = 0.68, col = col_from)
text(med["to_us"], 0.5, sprintf("leader visits the US: median %.1f years", med["to_us"]), pos = 4, cex = 0.68, col = col_to)
nl <- table(lag$direction[!is.na(lag$gap_years)])
title_left("Presidents travel sooner after a leader's visit than leaders come after a president's",
           sprintf("share of visits whose last visit the other way lies within the time on the x axis; %s presidential trips and %s leader visits with an earlier visit the other way",
                   fmt(nl[["from_us"]]), fmt(nl[["to_us"]])))
```

```{r lag-numbers, include = FALSE}
within1 <- function(d) mean(lag$gap_years[lag$direction == d] < 1, na.rm = TRUE)
```

When the president travels to a country, the last visit of that country's
leader to the US is a median of `r fmt(med[["from_us"]], 1)` years back
(`r pct(within1("from_us"))` within a year). A leader's visit to the US comes
a median of `r fmt(med[["to_us"]], 1)` years after the last presidential
visit to that country. These raw lags mix reciprocity with how often each
partner visits at all; the model below separates the two.

## Case-control design

The risk set follows the star. For a visit **to** the US, the controls are
other countries that could have sent their leader at that moment; for a
presidential visit, other countries the president could have gone to. We
sample each direction separately with `mode = "two"` (the US is the only
receiver of `to_us` visits and the only sender of `from_us` visits, so a
control changes only the partner) and `scope = "appearance"` (a country enters
the risk set after its first visit in that direction, which keeps out states
that do not exist yet). Five controls per visit.

```{r cc}
el <- ev[, c("sender", "receiver", "time")]
cc_to <- sample_non_events(el[ev$direction == "to_us", ], n_controls = 5, mode = "two",
                           scope = "appearance", seed = 1)
cc_fr <- sample_non_events(el[ev$direction == "from_us", ], n_controls = 5, mode = "two",
                           scope = "appearance", seed = 2)
cc_to$dir <- "to_us"; cc_fr$dir <- "from_us"
cc_fr$stratum <- cc_fr$stratum + max(cc_to$stratum)
cc <- rbind(cc_to, cc_fr)
c(strata = length(unique(cc$stratum)), rows = nrow(cc))
```

The statistics are computed for every row against the observed visits of both
directions (`history_log`), so a control is scored on the real history only.
Visits on the same day are not separated: a statistic counts earlier rows of
the same day. With daily dates and one visit per partner per day in all but
`r sum(duplicated(ev[c("partner", "time")]))` cases, this affects almost no
row.

```{r features}
cc <- endogenous_features(cc, history_log = el,
        stats = c("sender_outdegree", "receiver_indegree", "reciprocity_count",
                  "reciprocity_time_recent", "recency"))
to_us <- cc$dir == "to_us"
cc$inertia <- log1p(ifelse(to_us, cc$sender_outdegree, cc$receiver_indegree))  # partner's past visits, same direction
cc$recip <- log1p(cc$reciprocity_count)                                         # past visits in the other direction
cc$recip_recent <- transform_recency(cc$reciprocity_time_recent, half_life = 365.25)
cc$recip_recent[is.na(cc$recip_recent)] <- 0                                    # 1 just after a visit back, 0.5 after a year
cc$same_recent <- transform_recency(cc$recency, half_life = 365.25)
cc$same_recent[is.na(cc$same_recent)] <- 0
for (k in c("inertia", "recip", "recip_recent", "same_recent")) {
  cc[[paste0(k, "_to")]] <- cc[[k]] * to_us
  cc[[paste0(k, "_from")]] <- cc[[k]] * !to_us
}
```

## Linear model

Each statistic gets its own coefficient in each direction (a stratum holds
one direction only, so the direction itself cancels).

```{r clogit}
covs <- c("inertia_to", "recip_to", "recip_recent_to", "same_recent_to",
          "inertia_from", "recip_from", "recip_recent_from", "same_recent_from")
fit <- rem(reformulate(covs, response = "event"), data = cc, method = "clogit")
ct <- summary(fit$fit)$coefficients
est <- ct[, "coef"]; se <- ct[, "se(coef)"]
round(cbind(estimate = est, se = se), 2)
```

```{r forest, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Coefficients and 95% intervals of the four statistics, for visits to the US and presidential visits"}
lab <- c(inertia = "log(1 + past visits, same direction)", recip = "log(1 + past visits, other direction)",
         recip_recent = "recency of the last visit back (1 = just now)", same_recent = "recency of the last visit, same direction")
k <- c("inertia", "recip", "recip_recent", "same_recent")
par(mar = c(3.4, 15, 2.6, 1))
y <- c(4:1 + 0.15, 4:1 - 0.15)
e <- c(est[paste0(k, "_to")], est[paste0(k, "_from")]); s <- c(se[paste0(k, "_to")], se[paste0(k, "_from")])
plot(e, y, xlim = range(c(e - 2 * s, e + 2 * s, 0)), ylim = c(0.5, 4.5), type = "n", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
abline(v = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2)
cl <- rep(c(col_to, col_from), each = 4)
segments(e - 1.96 * s, y, e + 1.96 * s, y, col = cl, lwd = 2.2)
points(e, y, pch = 21, bg = "white", col = cl, cex = 1.3, lwd = 1.6)
axis(1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
axis(2, at = 4:1, labels = lab[k], las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.72, col.axis = ink, line = -0.6)
mtext("effect on the log-rate (95% interval)", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.72, col = ink_soft)
legend("bottomright", legend = c("partner's leader -> US", "US president -> partner"), col = c(col_to, col_from),
       lwd = 2.2, pch = 21, pt.bg = "white", bty = "n", cex = 0.72, text.col = ink)
title_left("What raises the rate of a visit to one partner rather than another",
           "conditional logit, five controls per visit")
```

```{r forest-numbers, include = FALSE}
hr <- function(n) exp(est[[n]])
```

For a visit to the US, each unit of `log(1 + the partner's earlier visits to
the US)` multiplies the rate by `r fmt(hr("inertia_to"), 2)`, and each unit
of `log(1 + earlier presidential visits to the partner)` by
`r fmt(hr("recip_to"), 2)`. A presidential visit in the past year raises the
rate of a visit back by a factor of `r fmt(hr("recip_recent_to"), 2)` at
recency 1. For presidential trips, the recency of the partner's last visit to
Washington multiplies the rate by `r fmt(hr("recip_recent_from"), 2)`, and the
president's own recent visit to the same country by
`r fmt(hr("same_recent_from"), 2)`.

## How fast reciprocity fades, and how inertia changes over the decades

The recency weight above fixes a one-year half-life. A smooth term lets the
data choose the shape: `nl()` of the log-time since the last visit in the
other direction, for visits with such a visit, next to an indicator for
partners without one. `tv(inertia)` lets the inertia effect change over the
75 years. The `gam` backend uses one control per visit.

```{r gam}
cc$gap <- log10(pmax(cc$reciprocity_time_recent, 1) / 365.25)    # log10 years
cc$never <- as.numeric(is.na(cc$gap))
cc$gap[is.na(cc$gap)] <- log10(80)
cc$year <- 1945.537 + cc$time / 365.25
w <- widen_case_control(cc, covariates = c("inertia", "gap", "never", "year"))
gfit <- rem(~ never + nl(gap, k = 6) + tv(inertia, k = 6), data = w, method = "gam", time = "year")
summary(gfit)$s.table
```

```{r smooth, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4.2, fig.alt = "Smooth effect of the time since the last visit in the other direction, and the time-varying inertia effect"}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(3.4, 3.6, 2.6, 1))
d1 <- smooth_data(gfit$fit, 1); d1 <- d1[d1$x < log10(75), ]
lo <- d1$fit - 1.96 * d1$se; hi <- d1$fit + 1.96 * d1$se
plot(d1$x, d1$fit, type = "n", ylim = range(lo, hi), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
abline(h = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2)
polygon(c(d1$x, rev(d1$x)), c(lo, rev(hi)), col = alpha(col_to, 0.18), border = NA)
lines(d1$x, d1$fit, col = col_to, lwd = 2.2)
at <- c(1 / 52, 1 / 12, 0.25, 1, 3, 10, 30)
axis(1, at = log10(at), labels = c("1 week", "1 month", "3 months", "1 year", "3 years", "10 years", "30 years"),
     tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.62, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
axis(2, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.72, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
mtext("time since the last visit in the other direction (log scale)", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.7, col = ink_soft)
mtext("effect on the log-rate", side = 2, line = 2.3, cex = 0.7, col = ink_soft)
title_left("Reciprocity fades after about a year", "smooth effect with 95% band; partners with a visit back only")
d2 <- smooth_data(gfit$fit, 2)
draw_smooth(d2, col = col_from, xlab = "year", ylab = expression(beta(t)~"of inertia"))
title_left("Inertia over time", "effect of log(1 + past visits, same direction)")
par(op)
```

```{r smooth-numbers, include = FALSE}
f_at <- function(d, x) approx(d$x, d$fit, xout = x)$y
drop_10 <- f_at(d1, log10(0.25)) - f_at(d1, log10(10))
b_early <- f_at(d2, 1960); b_late <- f_at(d2, 2010)
```

The smooth reciprocity effect falls by `r fmt(drop_10, 2)` on the log scale
between a visit back three months ago and one ten years ago. The inertia
coefficient is `r fmt(b_early, 2)` around 1960 and `r fmt(b_late, 2)` around
2010.

## What the design leaves out

- **Global effects.** Within a stratum every row has the same time, so a
  covariate that depends on time alone (the president in office, the year)
  cancels. The overall rate of visits in each presidency would need
  time-shifted sampling (`shift = "exponential"`); see the
  [email and the clock](case-email-global.html) case study.
- **Trips.** A presidential trip to several countries appears as several
  `from_us` events a few days apart; each is scored against the history before
  it, so the second stop of a trip sees the first.
